changed.context: Truth unknown; our support is small cases only. A circuit with NOT gates right on the promise is turned into one without, paying at most 2n - 5 more gates. changed.statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : List (Fin n × Fin n)) (v u w : Fin n) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), (∀ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ e.2) → (∀ a b c d : Fin n, a ≠ c → b ≠ d → ((a, b) ∈ E ∨ (b, a) ∈ E) → ((b, c) ∈ E ∨ (c, b) ∈ E) → ((c, d) ∈ E ∨ (d, c) ∈ E) → ((d, a) ∈ E ∨ (a, d) ∈ E) → False) → u ≠ w → ((v, u) ∈ E ∨ (u, v) ∈ E) → ((v, w) ∈ E ∨ (w, v) ∈ E) → (∀ z : Fin n, ((v, z) ∈ E ∨ (z, v) ∈ E) → z = u ∨ z = w) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v ∧ e.1 ≠ u ∧ e.2 ≠ u ∧ e.1 ≠ w ∧ e.2 ≠ w) → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => x e.1 && x e.2)) → (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 3 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v false e.1 && Function.update x v false e.2)) ∨ (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 4 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v true e.1 && Function.update x v true e.2))

changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 3) (v : Fin 4) => (363 : ℕ).testBit (4 * u.val + v.val)) 7
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 3 by 4 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 8 AND/OR gates for this graph that shares nothing; we hold none of 7; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 6 (on paper), a gap of 2. The checked twin merge reduces a square graph to a rectangular quotient, and we hold no table off the square beyond 2 by 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 2 left, 3 to 6 right, gate j writes wire 7 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 12 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: Find a binary AND/OR circuit below the monotone sparse-complement gate bound
changed.statement:
∃ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  let nbrR := fun (sourceRow : Fin n) => Finset.univ.filter (fun destCol : Fin m => G sourceRow destCol = false)
  let nbrC := fun (sourceCol : Fin m) => Finset.univ.filter (fun destRow : Fin n => G destRow sourceCol = false)
  (∀ a, 2 ≤ (nbrR a).card) ∧ (∀ c, 2 ≤ (nbrC c).card) ∧
  (∀ a b, a ≠ b → ((nbrR a) ∩ (nbrR b)).card ≤ 1) ∧
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C ∧
  (12 * C.size + 18 < 13 * (n + m) ∨
    ((∀ a, 3 ≤ (nbrR a).card) ∧ (∀ c, 3 ≤ (nbrC c).card) ∧
      12 * C.size + 14 < 13 * (n + m)))

changed.title: Find a bounded nonlinear-depth selector exceeding the two-binomial-sum rank budget
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depth := fun (w : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (C.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate w 0)).getD C.output 0
∃ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (u : Fin n) (v : Fin m),
  let entry := fun (a : Fin n) (b : Fin m) => if G a b then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0
  let A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) (ZMod 2) := fun i j =>
    entry i j + entry i v + entry u j + entry u v
  let represents := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C
  let budget := fun (t b : ℕ) =>
    (∑ j ∈ Finset.range b, Nat.choose (2*t) (j+1)) +
    (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (b-1), Nat.choose (2*t) (j+1))
  ∃ (d : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
    represents C ∧ depth (n+m) C ≤ d+1 ∧
    budget (C.gates.countP nonlinear) (2^d) < A.rank
changed.unlocks: tests the proposed rank budget at arbitrary nonlinear depth
changed.context: Try depth two with two nested nonlinear gates, allowing four unrelated raw affine taps. The budget is fourteen. On at least sixteen labels per bank seek at least fifteen independent rows after anchoring. Share free affine taps across banks, evaluate the table and row-reduce modulo two. Return the circuit and pivot positions. We hold no witness meeting this target.

changed.title: Fixed parity queries recover a paired-test graph exactly when witness differences admit a cover by classes without short odd zero sums
changed.statement:
∀ (n q rows cols pairs names messages : ℕ)
    (Y : Fin rows → Fin pairs → Bool → Fin names) (pass : Fin names → Bool)
    (col : Fin cols → Fin pairs → Bool → Bool) (pick : Fin rows → Fin pairs → Bool)
    (tag : Fin rows → Fin messages) (feature : Fin rows → Fin pairs → Fin n → ZMod 2),
  let V := Fin n → ZMod 2
  let edge := fun (r : Fin rows) (c : Fin cols) =>
    ∃ (z : Fin pairs) (p : Bool), pass (Y r z p) = true ∧ col c z p = true
  let seen := fun (r : Fin rows) (z : Fin pairs) => Y r z (pick r z)
  let direct := fun (r : Fin rows) (c : Fin cols) =>
    ∃ z, pass (seen r z) = true ∧ col c z (pick r z) = true
  let avail := fun (r : Fin rows) (c : Fin cols) (z : Fin pairs) =>
    col c z (!(pick r z)) = true
  let Need := {cell : Fin rows × Fin cols // edge cell.1 cell.2 ∧ ¬direct cell.1 cell.2}
  let conflict := fun (sel : Need → Fin pairs) (d : V) =>
    ∃ (t : Need) (r : Fin rows) (c : Fin cols) (z : Fin pairs),
      ¬edge r c ∧ avail r c z ∧ tag t.val.1 = tag r ∧
      seen t.val.1 (sel t) = seen r z ∧ feature t.val.1 (sel t) + feature r z = d
  (∃ (query : Fin q → (V →ₗ[ZMod 2] ZMod 2))
      (lookup : Fin messages → Fin names → (Fin q → ZMod 2) → Bool),
    ∀ (r : Fin rows) (c : Fin cols), edge r c ↔
      (direct r c ∨ ∃ z, avail r c z ∧
        lookup (tag r) (seen r z) (fun i => query i (feature r z)) = true)) ↔
  ∃ sel : Need → Fin pairs,
    (∀ t, avail t.val.1 t.val.2 (sel t)) ∧ ∃ parts : Fin q → Finset V,
      (∀ d, conflict sel d ↔ ∃ i, d ∈ parts i) ∧
      ∀ (i : Fin q) (s : Finset V), s ⊆ parts i → s.card ≤ n + 1 →
        s.card % 2 = 1 → (∑ v ∈ s, v) ≠ 0
changed.unlocks: Reduces the one-extra-parity question on the sixteen shift-12 columns to an affine span test, and gives an exact criterion when many positive columns or shared row messages must be served together.
changed.context: Choose an accepted mate per uncovered true cell. Every matching negative occurrence differs on some query. Put its difference in a class for a query taking value one. Conversely prescribe one on a basis taken from each class. A nonbasis vector with an even expansion gives an odd zero sum of size at most n+1. Extend the form linearly. Accept only the selected message, output and transcript triples. A negative match would give a class difference killed by every query. Details at f573a443dc, notes/seat-rlift-1/output-labels/parity-repair.md.

changed.title: Maximum joint agreement with disjoint products forces one fixed error word per block
changed.statement:
∀ (m r : ℕ), 0 < r →
  let V := Fin m × Fin r
  let W := V → Bool
  let low := fun (f : W → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset V), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card < r) ∧
      ∀ x, f x = (((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ a ∈ mon, x a = true)).card % 2) == 1)
  let prodBit := fun (x : W) (i : Fin m) => decide (∀ j : Fin r, x (i,j) = true)
  ∀ (P : Fin m → W → Bool), (∀ i, low (P i)) →
  ∀ e : Fin m → Bool,
    let err := fun (i : Fin m) (x : W) => xor (xor (prodBit x i) (P i x)) (e i)
    let hits := ((Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun x => ∀ i, err i x = false)).card
    let pointErrors := ∃ a : Fin m → Fin r → Bool, ∀ i x,
      err i x = decide (∀ j : Fin r, x (i,j) = a i j)
    (hits = (2^r - 1)^m ↔ pointErrors)
changed.unlocks: Identifies which individual prediction vectors saturate the volume bound used in covering-list estimates.
changed.context: Allowed monomials omit one bit in each block and span the cell. At equality they are independent. For coordinate error g and local bit x take a as the coefficient of the complementary local monomial in the correction. The Boolean polynomial (x+1+a)g has no full block and vanishes on the cell, hence everywhere. Every error forces x=1+a for every local bit. Each slice has odd error count so the forced word occurs. Multiply the allowed choices for the converse.
